findings.title: FSU did not exercise adequate due diligence or comply with certain procurement policies when it procured a new financial aid system. FSU subsequently determined it was not cost effective to continue using the system and opted to discontinue the contract resulting in the loss of all $680,000 expended on the system.
findings.description: FSU did not exercise adequate due diligence or comply with procurement policies when acquiring a new financial aid system, which FSU discontinued due to ongoing problems. The agency failed to prepare a sole source justification or solicit multiple vendors for implementation, resulting in a loss of $680,000.

dollar_amounts.context: loss of all expended on the system

findings.recommendation: FSU should comply with BOR policies and procedures when procuring future contracts and include a provision for liquidated damages in future contracts.

findings.title: FSU did not competitively procure student mental health services initially obtained without competition in October 2019 through an emergency procurement, and then extended multiple years using questionable sole source justifications. FSU also did not obtain required Board of Public Works approval when contract costs exceeded $1 million or ensure rates paid were consistent with the contract.
findings.description: FSU continued to use a vendor for student mental health services without competition or BPW approval after costs exceeded $1 million, and failed to verify rates against contracts. This resulted in overpayments of at least $9,600 during the audit period.
findings.recommendation: FSU should use a competitive procurement process for student mental health services, timely prepare and document justifications, obtain BPW approval when costs exceed $1 million, and recover all overpayments.

findings.title: FSU did not verify that its use of contracts procured by other entities was in the best interest of FSU as required by BOR procurement policies and procedures. FSU also did not verify that rates charged were consistent with the related contracts.
findings.description: FSU did not verify that using contracts from other entities was in its best interest or that rates charged were consistent with original contracts for four contracts totaling $7.6 million. This finding is repeated from the preceding audit report.

dollar_amounts.context: contracts entered into utilizing contracts procured by other entities
ICPA and MEEC contracts where rates not verified

findings.recommendation: FSU should document compliance with USM policies to verify that use of contracts is in the best interest of FSU and amounts invoiced are consistent with established contract rates.

findings.title: FSU had not established sufficient controls over student residency determinations and certain adjustments recorded in student accounts.
findings.description: FSU lacked independent reviews of initial residency determinations and changes, and output reports for non-cash credits were generated by employees responsible for posting them. Approximately $3.5 million in non-cash credits were recorded during fiscal year 2023 without adequate verification.

dollar_amounts.context: non-cash credits recorded during fiscal year 2023

findings.recommendation: FSU should ensure independent supervisory reviews of residency determinations and changes are conducted, and an independent verification of non-cash credit adjustments is performed.

findings.title: FSU did not ensure that all institutional aid awards, which were based in part on the student’s residency status, reflected the student’s actual residency status at the time of award. We identified incorrect awards totaling approximately $64,000.
findings.description: FSU did not verify residency status when making institutional aid awards, resulting in 13 students receiving incorrect awards based on their residency classification. Improper awards totaled approximately $54,650 with one student awarded $9,000 less than entitled.
findings.recommendation: FSU should ensure all institutional aid award amounts reflect the correct student residency status and review awarded aid for appropriate corrective action.

findings.title: FSU did not ensure that all critical payroll related transactions, including adjustments to employee leave balances and other earnings transactions, were independently reviewed for propriety.
findings.description: FSU failed to use output reports to verify leave balance adjustments or perform independent reviews of other earnings transactions. Two improper leave adjustments totaling 929 hours valued at approximately $24,000 were identified during testing.
findings.recommendation: FSU should use output reports to independently verify leave balance adjustments and perform independent supervisory reviews of other earnings transactions.

findings.title: FSU employees responsible for verifying that recorded collections were deposited also had access to the related collections prior to deposit.
findings.description: Employees responsible for verifying deposits had access to collections before deposit, creating a risk of undetected errors. Collections totaled approximately $25.6 million during fiscal year 2023.
findings.recommendation: FSU should ensure that an employee without access to collections verifies all recorded collections to deposit.

extraction.agency_response_summary: FSU generally agrees with the findings and recommendations but disagrees that a $680,000 loss was incurred in Finding 1 and disputes the existence of overpayments in Finding 2. The agency provided estimated completion dates for corrective actions on all recommendations.
extraction.extraction_notes: Prior finding number not explicitly stated in text for repeat finding.
